title: 2019 AMC 12B Problem 5
statement: Each piece of candy in a store costs a whole number of cents. Casper has exactly enough money to buy either \(12\) pieces of red candy, \(14\) pieces of green candy, \(15\) pieces of blue candy, or \(n\) pieces of purple candy. A piece of purple candy costs \(20\) cents. What is the smallest possible value of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(M\) be Casper’s money in cents. Since he can exactly buy \(12,\) \(14,\) or \(15\) whole-cent pieces, \(M\) is a multiple of \(\operatorname{lcm}(12,14,15)=420.\)

Purple candy costs \(20\) cents, so \(n=\dfrac{M}{20}.\) The smallest \(M\) is \(420,\) giving \(n=\dfrac{420}{20}=21.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Casper’s total money must be divisible by each candy count
The total is a multiple of \(\operatorname{lcm}(12,14,15)\)
